audit.why: Lucian out-ranging and out-trading Akshan in the shared band matches the kit: Lightslinger double-shots off every cast and Piercing Light is 500 range on a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Difficulty read stands; only the ability names were missing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes describe 'his E-dash reset' without the real number.
audit.why: Relentless Pursuit is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s and is shortened by every Lightslinger attack — the spike is that his dash is effectively always up once he has attack speed.
audit.corrected: First item: Relentless Pursuit (16s base) is refunded by Lightslinger hits, so the escape is permanently available.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ardent Blaze reveals enemies — the counter to Going Rogue — is never mentioned.
audit.why: Ardent Blaze (W, 14/13/12/11/10s, 900 range) marks and briefly reveals; that strips Akshan's camouflage and is why W is not a lane tool here. Lightslinger also empowers two attacks when a nearby enemy is immobilized, so any CC on you doubles his burst.
audit.corrected: Ardent Blaze reveals through Going Rogue; get immobilized near him and Lightslinger's next two shots come empowered.

edits.before: Bad news first: Lucian out-trades you in the range band you both fight in. His passive fires a second shot after every ability, so one Q from him becomes Q plus two empowered autos, and he does it from outside where your Avengerang comfortably connects. At Level 1, don't walk up to throw Q for a trade — last-hit with the tip of the boomerang and refuse the auto exchange. Your one mitigation early is your passive: landing your third hit on him procs the bonus magic damage and a short shield, so if you do trade, trade in bursts that cash that shield in rather than trickling single autos into his double-shot.
edits.after: Bad news first: Lucian out-trades you in the range band you both fight in. Lightslinger fires a second shot after every ability, so one Piercing Light becomes Q plus two empowered autos, and he does it from outside where your Avengerang comfortably connects. At Level 1, don't walk up to throw Q for a trade — last-hit with the tip of the boomerang and refuse the auto exchange. Your one mitigation early is Dirty Fighting: landing the third hit procs bonus damage and a short shield, so trade in bursts that cash that shield in rather than trickling single autos into his double-shot.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are where you claw back the trades you can't win standing still. The plan is the E-into-terrain Heroic Swing: bait his E dash first (he saves it to escape your Q follow-up), then swing off a wall, double-shot him, and Q on the way back. The catch is he can E-dash mid-swing, and your W (Going Rogue) camo is near-useless in open lane — it's a roam and reset tool here, not a trade button. At 6 your R can execute him because he's a squishy ADC, but you have to chunk him with Q-E first and land the channel before he dashes out of lock range; R finishes a fight you're already ahead in, it doesn't flip one he's winning.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are where you claw back the trades you can't win standing still. The plan is the terrain Heroic Swing: bait Relentless Pursuit first (16s at rank 1, and every Lightslinger hit shortens it), then swing off a wall, double-shot him, and Q on the way back. The catch is he can dash mid-swing, and Going Rogue camo is near-useless here — Ardent Blaze marks and reveals you through it, so treat W as a roam and reset tool, not a trade button. At 6 your R executes a squishy ADC, but chunk him with Q-E first and land the channel before he dashes out of lock range; R finishes a fight you lead, it doesn't flip one he's winning.
